daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The National Police are investigating allegations of wiretapping President Prabowo, with the police chief forming a special investigative team. The inquiry now includes possible treason charges, with legal experts urging authorities to apply sedition laws that carry the death penalty. Gerindra party has called for transparency in the investigation, while Irjen Slamet Uliandi has been named as a new suspect.

  • Vice President Ma'ruf Amin described President Prabowo's formation of BRAN (the National Research Agency) as akin to a "second proclamation."
  • The DPR has begun deliberations on the Asset Forfeiture Bill, targeting completion this month with a focus on corruption cases.
  • Minister Fadli Zon submitted recommendations for National Hero candidates to President Prabowo, including ten names such as the president's grandfather.
  • Partai Ummat has voiced support for the president's policies on supervising state budget usage.
  • The KPK seized Rp 2 billion from the KAI director in connection with corruption in a fuel station digitalization project.
  • A KPK employee is being questioned over alleged leaks of documents related to the ATR/BPN corruption case.
  • The Constitutional Court is hearing a challenge to the Tax Law calling for the elimination of taxes on sanitary pads.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Indonesian and U.S. navies conducted a joint commemorative dive to honor the USS Houston wreck site. Indonesia also opened its first language class in Tanzania, expanding cultural diplomacy in East Africa. At the IMO, Indonesia championed seafarer protection and maritime safety standards.

  • Indonesia highlighted cyber threats affecting the tourism sector at an ASEAN-Korea forum.
  • The Indonesian government declared the adoption of 18 children in Singapore to be illegal.
  • Indonesia's MER-C expanded medical services to southern Gaza through the Indonesia Medical Center.
  • TNI forces engaged in a firefight with OPM separatists in Yahukimo, seizing weapons and ammunition.

Other

Indonesia's economy grew 5.47 percent in the third quarter of 2026, with the finance minister emphasizing the role of state budget spending. Bank Indonesia forecasts that 2026 economic growth will reach between 4.9 and 5.7 percent. Meanwhile, Indef has warned of potential food price spikes ahead of Christmas and the 2027 New Year period.

  • Wildfire activity has surged in Central Kalimantan, with the national disaster agency reporting increased hotspots and Komnas HAM issuing six recommendations as fires reached 2,835 hectares.
  • Two soldiers died during firefighting operations in Kalimantan.
  • The Indonesian Navy traced 36 tons of seized gold concentrate back to Sumbawa.
  • Indonesia has designated 3.1 million hectares of waters for conservation purposes.
  • Authorities have targeted 39,923 accounts in a crackdown on online gambling.
